messages.text:
Good afternoon,

I received my Hammer Thor P2 this afternoon and noticed that the LCD screen
is damaged on the top left side. Despite the physical damage to the screen,
I was still able to successfully configure the device and add it to my
Bitcoin mining pool.

Please let me know how we can proceed with addressing the damaged screen.

Thank you,
Kevin P.
Handed to the team · Replacement screen part needs a person to arrange; I have no store or shipping t

Hi Kevin,

Thanks for the clear description, and good news first: what you are seeing is cosmetic only. The L. is a separate module from the hash board, and the fact that the Thor P2 booted, took your configuration and is already pushing shares to your pool tells me the board, the power supply and the network side are all healthy. Damage like this in the top corner of the display is almost always knocked loose or cracked in transit, and it has no effect on hashrate, temperatures or stability. The unit does not need to come back to us for it.

On my side I have recorded this as display damage in shipping rather than a hardware fault, and I have passed it to the team today so a colleague can sort the screen out with you directly. To make that quick, could you reply to this thread with two photos: one of the damaged area of the screen with the unit powered on, and one clear shot of the serial number label on the chassis. That lets them match the exact display revision for your unit the first time.

In the meantime you can keep it running as it is. If you want to watch it without the screen, the web interface on the miner's IP shows hashrate, chip temperature, fan speed and accepted shares in more detail than the LCD does anyway, so nothing is lost while the screen is being handled.

If you want to compare notes with other Thor P2 owners or ask something hardware-side outside of business hours, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hi Hal,

Thank you for the quick response. Other than the cosmetic defect on the LCD
screen, the Hammer Thor P2 is running great.

I have attached the requested photos of the damaged screen while powered on
and the serial number label on the chassis.

Thank you again for your assistance.

Best regards,
Kevin P.

Hi Kevin,

Thanks for sending these, and good to hear it is running well otherwise.

I opened the photo of the serial label and have the unit recorded as SN (number hidden), with the secondary sticker ···· next to it. Useful side benefit: that shot also shows a good part of the board around the label, and everything there looks clean. No cracked traces, no lifted components, no stress marks around the mounting posts or the display standoff. That matches what the unit is doing in practice and confirms the impact was taken by the display module alone.

One thing to flag honestly: only the serial photo came through on my side, the shot of the powered on screen did not attach. There is nothing urgent about it, but if you can reply to this thread with that one image when you get a moment, it completes the record for the display, since the exact damage pattern tells us which display revision and bracket the unit has.

Nothing changes for you in the meantime. Keep it mining as it is. The L. is driven over a small ribbon off the controller, so a damaged panel cannot affect clock speed, chip voltage or share submission, and your pool side stats remain the authoritative reading. If you ever want finer detail than the panel gives, the web interface on the miner's IP shows per chip temperature, fan RPM and accepted versus rejected shares.

The screen itself sits with the team now, and they are back Monday at 10am ET, with their answer coming to you in this thread. If you want to talk hardware over the weekend, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hi Hal H. are additional pics of the screen, let me know if they do not send

Thank you again,

Kevin

Hi Kevin,

Thanks for trying again, and sorry to be the bearer of this one: the new images did not come through on my side either. All I have on the thread is the earlier shot of the serial label and the board around it. Something between your mail client and ours is dropping the attachments, which happens most often when the photos go out at full phone resolution.

Two things usually get around it. First, send them one per email rather than several in one message, which keeps each one well under the size limit. Second, if your phone offers a smaller or medium size when attaching, pick that, or take a screenshot of the photo and send the screenshot instead, since a screenshot is a fraction of the original file size and is still plenty of detail for a cracked panel.

That said, please do not spend your evening fighting with it. The photos are useful for the record, not a condition for anything. What matters is already established and written down against your unit: the display took the damage in transit, the serial is (number hidden), the board is visibly clean, and the miner is hashing normally on your pool. Nothing about the screen limits what the unit does, so keep it running exactly as it is.

The display side sits with the team, and they are back Monday at 10am ET, with their reply coming to you in this thread. If you would rather drop the photos somewhere instant over the weekend, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there. Images post straight into the chat there without any mail size limits.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thank you Hal,

Sending just one pic this time.

Thanks,

Kevin

Hi Kevin,

Still nothing on my side, so let us stop there. That is three attempts, and whatever is stripping the attachments is sitting between your mail client and our thread, not with you. I am not going to keep sending you back for another one.

The important part is that we do not actually need the photo to move this along. Your own description is clear, you told us at the start that the damage is on the top left of the LCD and that the unit configured and joined your pool normally, and the serial photo that did arrive gave us (number hidden) plus a clean view of the surrounding board. That is enough to have it on record as transit damage to the display module with the miner itself intact, which is exactly how it is written down.

So nothing further is needed from you tonight. Leave the Thor P2 mining as it is over the weekend. A damaged panel has no path to affect hashrate, chip temperature or share submission, and your pool dashboard remains the true reading of what the unit is producing.

The display sits with the team and they are back Monday at 10am ET, with their reply arriving in this thread. If you do want to get the photos in front of someone sooner, our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf takes images straight into the chat with no mail limits, and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hal,

Thank you again, we definitely gave it best efforts for sure.

I'll be out of the country this coming week but still able to reply to any
emails.

Thank you again for the assistance,

Kevin

Hi Kevin,

We did, and I appreciate you going round three times on it. The record is complete enough without it.

Noted that you are out of the country this week and reachable by email. That works fine here, since everything left on this is on our side and the thread follows you. Nothing further is needed from you while you travel.

One small thing worth knowing while the unit runs unattended: the Thor P2 picks its network back up on its own after a power blip or a router reboot, so you should not need to touch anything. The easiest way to confirm it is still working from abroad is your pool dashboard rather than the miner itself. If the worker shows as active with shares coming in, the unit is fine. A worker that goes quiet usually means the house internet or power dropped rather than the miner failing, and in that case it will rejoin by itself once the connection is back.

The display is with the team, they are back Monday at 10am ET, and their reply will land in this thread wherever you are. Safe travels, and if a hardware question comes up while you are away, the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is the quickest route, with JD as @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hal,

Thank you so much,

Kevin

Hi Kevin,

My pleasure. Enjoy the trip, and enjoy watching that Thor P2 stack shares while you are away.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Note to the team: A thumbs up reaction, nothing to answer. The thread is closed out on my side: the display damage is recorded against serial (number hidden) on Shop···· as a non fault, the miner is hashing normally, and the screen itself is with the team for Monday. No reply sent.
